correctness.rationale: A deletion from any maximal constant run gives one unique descendant. The only new prohibited palindromes must straddle the deletion site, yielding the two explicit outer-letter comparison tests. Six equality-pattern states, each with six labeled realizations, track and weight all such valid deletions without duplicates. Symbolic exact algebra proves the rational G(z,u); the recurrence from its denominator and six explicit initial polynomials proves the maximum and all maximizing counts for every n. A standalone verification script reconstructs the transfer, confirms the symbolic identity, independently enumerates actual deletion outputs through n=13, and checks recurrence through n=26. No numerical experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a canonical finite-type, three-palindrome-avoiding coding language, the number of distinct reads surviving one deletion without violating the output constraint is a meaningful neighborhood invariant: it measures surviving synchronization-read diversity. The complete all-length bivariate law and sharp three-residue maximum/multiplicities provide information inaccessible from ordinary source counting or unrestricted run-count deletion sizes, with nontrivial transfer and boundary analysis. This is a self-contained quantitative benchmark; no unproven code-capacity gain is asserted.
